title: abhiṇhapaccavekkhitabbaṭhāna sutta
credit: Pāḷi text and English translation as in Mor’s Pāḷi Workshop booklet.
groupSub: Reflecting upon and Examining the Dhamma

paras.en:
“Bhikkhus, there are these five themes that should frequently be reflected upon by a woman or a man,
by a householder or one gone forth.
What five?

(1) A woman or a man, a householder or one gone forth, should frequently reflect thus:
‘I am subject to old age; I am not exempt from old age.’

(2) A woman or a man, a householder or one gone forth, should frequently reflect thus:
‘I am subject to illness; I am not exempt from illness.’

(3) A woman or a man, a householder or one gone forth, should frequently reflect thus:
‘I am subject to death; I am not exempt from death.’

(4) A woman or a man, a householder or one gone forth, should frequently reflect thus:
‘I must be parted and separated from everyone and everything dear and agreeable to me.’

(5) A woman or a man, a householder or one gone forth, should frequently reflect thus:
‘I am the owner of my kamma, the heir of my kamma;
I have kamma as my origin, kamma as my relative, kamma as my refuge; whatever kamma I will do,
good or bad, of that I will be the heir.’”
